about.title: Personal Injury Help in Placerville, California
about.longDescription: Placerville may be a small Gold Country city of roughly 10,650 people, but its roads carry a steady stream of traffic, and collisions happen. Public records show 31 injury collisions in the most recent final year, with 51 people hurt and 1 traffic death. Corridors like Rt 50, US-50, Placerville Drive, and Broadway Drive account for a large share of reported crashes, and reports tend to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, you may be dealing with medical bills, missed work, and uncertainty about what comes next. We provide free case reviews — our team handles personal injury claims and can review the details of what happened. There's no cost to reach out, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Contacting us costs nothing and can help you understand your options before time limits under California law start working against you.

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Shared Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life, so your losses beyond medical bills can still count.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Win
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Placerville?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit for most personal injury claims. If a government agency, like a city or county entity, was involved, the notice period can be as short as six months. It's wise to act sooner rather than later so evidence and deadlines don't work against you.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. We can help sort out how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Placerville?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Rt 50, US-50, Placerville Drive, and Broadway Drive account for a notable share of reported injury collisions, with activity peaking on Thursdays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply where collision counts are highest on record, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. In standard personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and emotional distress. Compensation depends on the facts of your case rather than a fixed limit.
